thread:
Alice Ng: Quick follow-up from the postmortem — we've had 3 OOM spikes in prod over the last 5 days, all on tail-heavy transform requests (seq len ~1024). Runtime allocator shows high per-shard fragmentation. I want one consolidated action list: profiling, short-term limits, GC tuning, and recurring alerting. @Bob Carter @Carol Li @Dave K @Emily R please ack and add owners/timelines.

Bob Carter: Ack. Priority P0 for Dedicated customers. My proposals: (1) immediate safety net (per-request memory cap + reject above threshold), (2) full heap sampling on a canary pool, (3) GC pacing change trial (lower interval). I can own 1 and 3. ETA: safety net by EOD tomorrow, GC trial next week.

Carol Li: I can take profiling (2). I'll schedule continuous heap sampling on 2 canary nodes and push flame graphs to the incident folder. ETA: sampling live in 6 hours, initial flames by EOD.

Dave K: Noted. From prior traces I suspect allocator fragmentation inside the slab allocator under mixed short/long sequences. Proposed runtime changes: add a per-shard compacting pass after idle windows, and expose a jemalloc background_purge toggle. I can prototype the compacting pass this week. Also adding a runtime flag to cap per-request KV prefetch size would help.

Emily R: From SRE side: we need clearer alerting — current OOM alert noisy and only fires after OOM. Requesting two things: (A) proactive memory-pressure alert at 75% reserved memory, (B) a recurring weekly OOM trend dashboard. I'll create the alerts and dashboard. ETA: alerts by tomorrow, dashboard v1 by Friday.

infra-bot: [alert] OOM anomaly detected on rdp-node-42 (2026-03-21 18:23:11) — context: 3x OOMs in 48h. Link: https://redwood-monitoring/alerts/oom-2026-03-21

Alice Ng: Good. I'll collate into a small action tracker and assign owners + dates here. Also: please add PR links to the tracker when you have them.

Alice Ng: ACTION LIST (initial):
- ACTION 1: Safety net (per-request memory cap + reject path) — owner: Bob Carter — ETA: 2026-03-24 EOD — status: in progress
- ACTION 2: Heap sampling + flame graphs on canary — owner: Carol Li — ETA: 2026-03-23 EOD — status: sampling live
- ACTION 3: GC pacing trial (tune background purge) — owner: Bob Carter — ETA: 2026-03-30 — status: planned
- ACTION 4: Runtime slab compact pass prototype — owner: Dave K — ETA: 2026-03-27 — status: working
- ACTION 5: Alerting + OOM trend dashboard weekly — owner: Emily R — ETA: 2026-03-24 — status: in progress
- ACTION 6: Per-request KV prefetch cap flag — owner: Dave K — ETA: 2026-03-28 — status: planned

Bob Carter: I'll open the safety-net PR today. Minimal config: 
```yaml
requests: 
  memory_cap_mb: 8000
  reject_on_exceed: true
```
I'll add unit tests and a canary rollout.

Carol Li: Sampling running. First flame graph uploaded: https://internal-storage/oom-profiles/176370-sample-1.svg. Early notes: high retained slab segments pinned by long-lived cache entries + growth spikes during batched requests.

Dave K: Seeing the flame — yep, looks like long-lived KV slices pinned across shards. I'll add the compact pass to the runtime and try a background --purge=aggressive on canary. Will link PR here when ready.

Emily R: Alerts created: mem_pressure_75 and mem_spike_rate. Added a weekly dashboard tile for OOM count + top 10 offenders by route. Linking: https://grafana/redwood/d/oom-trends

Bob Carter: Quick Q: do we want auto-fallback to smaller model variant on memory pressure? That could avoid hard rejects for some customers. Thoughts?

Alice Ng: Good idea. Let's make it optional for Dedicated customers. New ACTION: fallback routing on memory pressure — owner: Alice Ng (product coord) — ETA: 2026-04-03 — status: triage.

Carol Li: FYI I'll correlate flame data with request traces and attach span IDs so runtime owners can map to code paths.

Dave K: Accepted. I'll prioritize compact pass and prefetch cap over further changes. If compacting reduces fragmentation by 30% we may be able to relax caps.

Emily R: Can we cadence a 15-min sync tomorrow to confirm sampling results? I can host.

Alice Ng: Yes — 15:30 UTC tomorrow works for me. Meeting invite to follow. Please update the tracker with PR links and short notes.

Bob Carter: :thumbsup: will update PR link and add canary rollout plan.

Carol Li: :thumbsup: flames and trace correlation added.

Dave K: :thumbsup: prototyping now.

Emily R: :thumbsup: alerts in prod monitor.

Alice Ng: Thanks all. I'll post a final consolidated follow-up doc after tomorrow's sync. If anyone hits blockers before then ping me directly.
